payload.reason: The evidence suggests that differences in cloudiness and precipitation between the Elwha and Quinault valleys influence solar radiation absorption and glacier dynamics, supporting the idea that orientation and environmental factors affect glacier distribution.

claims.text: The Elwha valley is expected to receive more solar radiation due to being less cloudy than the Quinault valley, which can enhance glacier melt.
Spatially variable precipitation influences glacier extent, indicating that the orientation of the grid and associated climatic conditions affect glacier distribution.
Cloudiness patterns, influenced by topography, affect the amount of solar radiation reaching glaciers, impacting their mass balance and distribution.
Differences in precipitation, rather than valley morphology, are the main cause of the different extents of glaciers in the Elwha and Quinault areas.
